framework.name: react-router
framework.notes: React Router v7 framework mode (SSR), declared as ^7.16.0, served by a hand-written Express 5 server (server/app.ts + server/index.ts) instead of the default React Router server. Routing is file-based via react-router-auto-routes (app/routes.ts, autoRoutes()); not a Next.js app/pages router. Legacy Remix packages remain: @remix-run/server-runtime ^2.17.4, remix-auth ^4.2.0, remix-auth-github, remix-utils, @nasa-gcn/remix-seo. Docs still call it Remix (docs/features.md).

monorepo.notes: Single package (private, name epic-stack-template). No workspaces field, no pnpm-workspace.yaml. remix.init/ carries its own package.json + lockfile but is a template-init helper, not a workspace.

auth.notes: Self-managed auth: cookie sessions (createCookieSessionStorage, cookie name en_session, sameSite lax, httpOnly) + bcryptjs password hashing + @epic-web/totp 2FA + @simplewebauthn passkeys (registration/authentication routes) + email verification (6-digit code or link) backed by the Verification model. OAuth via remix-auth + remix-auth-github; GitHub is the ONLY provider wired (app/utils/connections.server.ts). Rate-limited auth paths plus honeypot fields; CSRF tokens were deliberately removed (docs/decisions/035-remove-csrf.md). RBAC = Role/Permission rows enforced by requireUserWithRole / requireUserWithPermission.

i18n.notes: No i18n library and no translation files; English strings are inline. intl-parse-accept-language is used only to derive the user time zone (app/utils/client-hints.tsx), not for translations. docs/features.md lists internationalization as future work.

payments.notes: No payment SDK and no webhook route anywhere; no STRIPE_* env var. docs/features.md lists Stripe ecommerce support as future work.

email.notes: Plain fetch() to https://api.resend.com/emails (app/utils/email.server.ts) with React Email rendering via @react-email/components. 3 templates: signup email verification (app/routes/_auth/signup.tsx), password reset (app/routes/_auth/forgot-password.tsx), change-email confirmation (app/routes/settings/profile/change-email.server.tsx). Hardcoded sender hello@epicstack.dev. RESEND_API_KEY is optional in the zod env schema (emails are logged instead when unset).

routes.notes: 45 route modules (plus 3 _layout files = 48 files under app/routes/, per the git tree). URL paths derived from react-router-auto-routes conventions (_auth/_marketing/_seo are pathless layouts, [.] escapes dots, $param -> :param, trailing _ unstacks password_.create). There is no /api/* namespace: server endpoints live under /resources/* plus /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml and the /webauthn/* action routes.

env.notes: .env.example ships 19 names (placeholders / MOCK_* values only, no real secrets). The app zod schema in app/utils/env.server.ts also has 19; of these the five Tigris/AWS vars are NOT optional (the app throws without them) while SENTRY_DSN, RESEND_API_KEY and GITHUB_* are optional. The container additionally injects LITEFS_DIR, DATABASE_FILENAME, CACHE_DATABASE_FILENAME, INTERNAL_PORT, FLY, PRISMA_SCHEMA_DISABLE_ADVISORY_LOCK (other/Dockerfile) and LiteFS needs FLY_CONSUL_URL, PRIMARY_REGION, HOSTNAME (other/litefs.yml). CI supplies FLY_API_TOKEN as a GitHub secret. Nothing is required at build time: the typecheck CI job runs npm run build BEFORE copying .env, and the Dockerfile build needs only an optional SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN build secret.

deploy.notes: Dockerfile lives at other/Dockerfile (fly.toml sets dockerfile=/other/Dockerfile, ignorefile=/other/Dockerfile.dockerignore) and its header says the file is moved to the repo root before building. Container CMD is litefs mount (FUSE + Fly consul lease), which then runs other/litefs.yml exec: prisma migrate deploy -> WAL pragmas -> prisma generate --sql -> npm start. The app process listens on PORT=8081 inside the container behind the LiteFS proxy on INTERNAL_PORT=8080 (= fly.toml internal_port; health checks /resources/healthcheck and /litefs/health). Deploy is flyctl-only from GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/deploy.yml: container + deploy jobs on push to dev/main, staging and production Fly apps named from fly.toml). No docker-compose, no Vercel/Docker-Swarm config. standalone_output is a Next.js concept and does not apply (false).

tests.notes: Vitest config lives in vite.config.ts (include ./app/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}, globalSetup tests/setup/global-setup.ts, v8 coverage). 7 unit test files (app/**/*.test.*): auth.server, headers.server, misc.error-message, misc.use-double-check, sentry-event-filters, routes/_auth/auth.$provider/callback, routes/users/$username/index. 8 Playwright specs in tests/e2e (2fa, error-boundary, note-images, notes, onboarding, passkey, search, settings-profile) with image fixtures and test helpers. tests/setup/setup-test-env.ts loads .env via dotenv and makes console.error/console.warn THROW. CI is a single workflow with 5 jobs (lint, typecheck, vitest, playwright, container) plus a deploy job; each job copies .env.example to .env and runs prisma migrate deploy first. scripts.validate = run-p test lint typecheck test:e2e:run.

vendor.name: fly.io
vendor.what_it_does: hosting/PaaS: internal port 8080, volumes, health checks, fly-client-ip rate-limit key, flyctl deploys of staging + production apps
vendor.swap_target_hint: any Docker host / VPS / Railway / Render (drop LiteFS for a single instance)

vendor.name: litefs
vendor.what_it_does: SQLite replication + leases via Fly consul; container entrypoint is litefs mount and the app talks to the primary over Fly internal networking
vendor.swap_target_hint: none (single-instance SQLite) or Postgres with real replication

vendor.name: tigris (S3-compatible object storage)
vendor.what_it_does: profile-photo and note-image storage plus serving optimized images; hand-rolled AWS SigV4 signing (no AWS SDK dependency)
vendor.swap_target_hint: any S3-compatible endpoint (R2/MinIO/AWS S3) by changing AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 + bucket secrets

pitfalls.detail: Runtime env is validated with zod in app/utils/env.server.ts and throws on missing variables; DATABASE_PATH, DATABASE_URL, SESSION_SECRET, HONEYPOT_SECRET, INTERNAL_COMMAND_TOKEN, CACHE_DATABASE_PATH and all five Tigris vars (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_REGION, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3, BUCKET_NAME) are NOT optional, so the app will not boot without storage credentials even if you never upload a file. app/utils/session.server.ts also calls process.env.SESSION_SECRET.split(',') at import time, which crashes the process with an unhelpful TypeError when SESSION_SECRET is unset. Copy .env.example to .env first. Build time is fine: CI builds before copying .env.

No postinstall script in the repo, but Prisma client generation is required before dev/build/typecheck: run npx prisma generate (and npx prisma generate --sql for the TypedSQL searchUsers query) or imports of #app/utils/db.server.ts and @prisma/client/sql fail. npm run setup bundles build + migrate deploy + generate --sql + playwright install.

sharp (^0.34.5, image optimization) and @sentry/profiling-node (^10.38.0) ship platform-specific native binaries; unusual platforms or Node ABIs fail at install or first run. bcryptjs (pure JS) avoids a node-gyp build, so no C toolchain is needed otherwise.

.npmrc pins legacy-peer-deps=true, i.e. upstream accepts unresolved peer ranges (React 19 alongside remix-auth-github/remix-utils). npm install works with it; pnpm/yarn or a flagless npm ci can fail on peer resolution.

docs/features.md claims SQLite caching is done with better-sqlite3 and that the framework is Remix; the code uses node:sqlite (DatabaseSync) and React Router v7, and better-sqlite3 is not a dependency at all.

docs/security.md and docs/troubleshooting.md tell you to edit contentSecurityPolicy directives or remove reportOnly: true in server/index.ts, but that block no longer exists there: headers now come from @nichtsam/helmet defaults plus a hand-written nonce, so an agent following those docs hunts for configuration that was moved or removed.

docs/getting-started.md still describes npx epicli new / create-remix --template workflows, and a leftover remix.init/ directory (364-line index.mjs that rewrites fly.toml, package.json and .env.example and prompts interactively) is still in the repo even though this repo IS the template (private, name epic-stack-template).

Four of the five marketing routes are one-line stubs (About page, etc.) and the home page is a marketing page for the Epic Stack itself; the only real product surface is notes plus settings under /users/:username/notes. Anything expecting a working dashboard must build it.

The production image entrypoint is litefs mount (FUSE plus a Fly consul lease) with migrations executed by other/litefs.yml on the primary candidate. docker run of the built image will not start the app locally without /dev/fuse and LiteFS/consul env, and the app port (8081) sits behind the LiteFS proxy (8080), so naive port mapping hits the wrong process.
pitfalls.evidence: other/Dockerfile (CMD litefs mount, PORT/INTERNAL_PORT), other/litefs.yml, fly.toml

pitfalls.detail: Tests need .env: tests/setup/setup-test-env.ts imports dotenv/config and app/utils/env.server.ts before anything else, and it monkey-patches console.error/console.warn to THROW, so incidental React or React Router warnings surface as hard test failures. Playwright needs browsers installed (npm run test:e2e:install) and the app built (pretest:e2e:run runs npm run build).

Local dev is mock-first: npm run dev sets MOCKS=true and MSW intercepts Resend, GitHub OAuth, Tigris and pwned-passwords. GITHUB_* values must be prefixed MOCK_ (and AWS_* can be fake) or the code calls the real APIs on login/upload.

node:sqlite requires Node >= 22.5 and engines requires ^22.18.0; older Node lacks DatabaseSync entirely (cache.server.ts, tests/setup/db-setup.ts). Docker (node:22-bookworm-slim) and CI (node 22) match.

verdict.best_for: A production-shaped single-tenant web app that needs real auth (password + 2FA + passkeys + GitHub SSO), RBAC, file uploads, transactional email and a SQLite database, deployed as your own Docker container.
verdict.weak_for: Multi-tenant SaaS that needs billing, i18n/RTL, Postgres scale-out, background jobs or edge/serverless hosting - none of that exists here, and the Fly.io + LiteFS + Tigris coupling is opinionated.
verdict.swap_burden: heavy - auth is hand-rolled and correct but is entwined with sessions/verification/permissions, and hosting is woven through the Dockerfile, litefs.yml, fly.toml, CI, the rate limiter (fly-client-ip) and storage (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3), so dropping Fly means rewriting the deploy layer plus the storage signature code.
